author: Mark Atwood
text:
Closed via calendars-server + contacts-server propagation. Chat-server propagation deferred to bd:JMAP-ic0j.76 (human-label) because two existing chat-server integration tests pin the MAY-path behavior with spec-citation assertion comments; switching chat-server requires a human decision about whether those tests' intent should change.

Changes landed (this bead):

1. crate-jmap-calendars-server/src/memory.rs get_changes destroy arm:
   - OLD: `fates.insert(id.clone(), IdFate::Destroyed)` unconditionally
   - NEW: `match fates.remove(id) { Some(IdFate::Created) => {} /* omit */ Some(_) | None => { fates.insert(id.clone(), IdFate::Destroyed); } }`
   - Mirrors canonical jmap-mail-server crate-jmap-mail-server/src/memory/mod.rs:670-680.
   - bd:JMAP-ic0j.15 recycling-detection invariant preserved via a new `ever_destroyed: HashSet<Id>` that the debug_assert! consults independently of the dedup state (necessary because the SHOULD-preferred destroy arm removes the Created fate, so a later recycled create would not find the Destroyed sentinel the old assertion relied on).

2. crate-jmap-calendars-server/src/memory.rs dedup_pass_does_not_panic_on_distinct_recreated_ids test:
   - Updated assertion to assert destroyed.is_empty() (was vec![id_a]).
   - Oracle citation in the test comment: RFC 8620 §5.2 verbatim 'If a record was created and then destroyed within the window … the server SHOULD remove the id from the response entirely.'

3. crate-jmap-contacts-server/src/memory.rs get_changes destroy arm:
   - Vec-based path-2 → path-1 conversion. Added a `was_created_in_window` local before the retain so the post-retain destroyed-push check can skip when the destroy is paired with an in-window create.

4. Filed bd:JMAP-ic0j.76 (P3, human-label) for chat-server propagation deferral. The two conflicting tests are:
   - crate-jmap-chat-server/tests/integration.rs:1435-1449 message_set_burn_on_read_fires_on_read_at
   - crate-jmap-chat-server/tests/integration.rs:1665-1679 (message expiry sibling)

Verification (cargo workspace pre-commit gate):
- cargo fmt --all: clean
- cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings: clean
- cargo test --workspace: all passing (0 failed across every test result line); calendars-server's dedup_pass_does_not_panic_on_distinct_recreated_ids now passes with the new SHOULD-preferred assertion; the two debug_assert! recycling-detection tests still trip correctly via the ever_destroyed set.
